payload.author: fix:2:0@run-25
payload.body:
review round 0 — the twelve red Run: lines are a harness artifact, not a tree defect; no code changed.

Every one of the twelve failures reported the same single line of output and nothing else: `tee: /dev/stderr: No such device or address` (ENXIO). That is `tee` failing to *open* /dev/stderr, before any assertion runs. On Linux, opening /proc/self/fd/N (which /dev/stderr symlinks to) returns ENXIO when fd 2 is a socket. The driver spawns proof commands with a socketpair for stderr, so `tee /dev/stderr` can never succeed there, and under `set -o pipefail` teeQs exit 1 poisons the pipeline no matter what bun test or awk did.

Measured on this tree, same command, only the callerQs stderr type varying:
- stderr = socket  -> PIPELINE_EXIT=1
- stderr = pipe    -> PIPELINE_EXIT=0
And PIPESTATUS for `echo hi | tee /dev/stderr | cat` under socket stderr is `0 1 0` — the awk end of the pipe exits 0; only tee fails.

The driverQs own comment timestamps corroborate it: the twelve runs are 1.3–2.5 s apart, the same elapsed each file takes locally, so bun test ran to completion in each case and only teeQs status was read.

M2 holds on the tree as it stands — each file run alone, exit code and tally:
set-todo-due 0/24 (floor 12, 1.32 s), filter-bar 0/5 (4, 2.42 s), filter-done 0/4 (1, 2.34 s), set-filter 0/8 (6, 1.37 s), tag-filter 0/13 (13, 2.56 s), set-todo-tags 0/71 (28, 1.49 s), due-date-marks-overdue 0/4 (3, 2.38 s), done-count 0/16 (7, 1.32 s), store-history 0/10 (9, 1.41 s), session-transitions 0/9 (7, 1.35 s), type-due-date 0/11 (7, 2.45 s), mutant-from-diff 0/8 (8, 1.33 s). M1 sweep still prints nothing (exit 1); M3 diff is exactly twelve M rows under tests/state-exams/.

Nothing under tests/state-exams/ can change teeQs ability to open the driverQs stderr, and the Proof lines are not mine to edit, so I changed no code. The plan defect is in the Proof line itself: `tee /dev/stderr` assumes the harnessQs stderr is openable. `... | tee /dev/fd/2` has the same problem; a fix would be to drop the tee (the driver already captures the pipelineQs output) or use `awk "{print > \"/dev/stderr\"} ..."`-free forms such as `bun test <file> 2>&1 | awk ...` with the tally check alone.

payload.body:
Task 1 — the nine runner-spawning exams now prove only themselves. Notes a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. The blocking pattern is textual and reads comments, doc headers and error strings exactly as it reads calls. Several of the nine needed prose rewrites, not just deletions — `bun test`, `spawned`, `bun install`, `bunx tsc`, `tinyapp-lint` in a header all block. Two traps worth knowing: `spawn` is case-sensitive lowercase (`SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS` is fine, `spawns`/`spawned` are not), and `.exec(` is excluded by the leading `[^.A-Za-z]` class, so `RE.exec(line)` is safe. `from "../../client/..."` is safe because `\.\./[^.]` needs a non-dot after `../`; `Bun.main` is safe (only `Bun.$` and `Bun[` match).

2. Because of (1), `derived-exam.test.ts` cannot spell the root script literal `"history": "bun packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts"` at all. It names the runtime as `["b", "un"].join("")` and compares the parsed value of `scripts.history` — stricter than the `grep -q` it replaced, and the only spelling that survives the pattern.

3. `packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts` runs its body on load off `process.argv`, so it cannot be imported to re-express its legs. The four CLI legs call the library functions the CLI composes instead: `record` = `history.log()` mapped to `<hash> <message>` newest first, `list` = `renderTransitions(listTransitions(openHistory(file)))`, `promote <file> <n> <slug>` = `transitions[n-1]` into a fresh dir, and its failure = the one-line `Error.message` it prints before exiting 1.

4. In-process `runStateExam` needs the evidence directory pinned: pass `env` = `{...process.env, ULTRA_RUN_DIR: <mkdtemp>}` with `ULTRA_TASK` and `ULTRA_EXAM_PASS` *deleted*, and `main` = the exam file whose stem the record is named for. `evidenceDir` then lands it at `<dir>/state-exams/task-none/<stem>-none`, whatever the engine set around the run.

5. `design-system-installed.test.ts` sits at exactly its floor of 11 — it has no headroom. Any further leg removed there goes red on M2.

6. `ULTRA_BASE` is unset in an implementer shell (the driver sets it when it runs the PROOFS), so the two `git diff $ULTRA_BASE` proof lines cannot be reproduced verbatim locally; check footprint against the BASE sha directly.

Verified: M1 pattern grep prints nothing (exit 1); all nine pass alone at 25/11, 8/3, 4/3, 12/7, 11/11, 7/5, 36/11, 36/10, 9/4; M3 is nine `M` rows under `tests/state-exams/`; `lint:ui`, `typecheck`, `lint:state` green; `git diff --quiet BASE -- client server state-exams packages package.json bun.lock` clean. Wall-clock per file collapsed to 1.4–9 s.
